summary.short: Creates a Dyslexia Research Grant Program run by the State Department of Education, awarding grants to Nebraska-based private businesses researching AI-based writing assistance for individuals with dyslexia, capped at $500,000 in total. Grant money must be used only for that research; misuse leads to Attorney General civil recovery.
summary.long: Section 2 of the Nebraska act creates a Dyslexia Research Grant Program administered by the State Department of Education. Eligible applicants are privately owned businesses based in Nebraska that are researching AI-based writing assistance for individuals with dyslexia (subsection 1). Applicants apply to the department on a prescribed form, and grants are conditioned on compliance with the section; the department may award grants to any eligible applicant (subsection 3). Total grants may not exceed $500,000, and the Legislature intends funding from the Education Future Fund. Grant money may be used only to research AI-based writing assistance by individuals with dyslexia, focused on aggregate writing analytics that teachers can use to develop comprehensive literacy plans for students with dyslexia (subsection 4). If grant money is used in violation, the department notifies the Attorney General, who must bring a civil action to recoup the money; recovered funds are remitted to the State Treasurer for the Education Future Fund (subsection 5). The State Board of Education may adopt rules to carry out the section (subsection 6). The provided document contains only this section, and no effective date appears in it.

notes: Partial text: this is Sec. 2 only. The enacting bill and the other sections of the act are not in the document, so the registry title (Teacher Incentive Programs) is not reflected in this section, which creates only the Dyslexia Research Grant Program. The text sets an aggregate cap of five hundred thousand dollars on all grants (Sec. 2(3)(c)) and states legislative intent that grants be funded from the Education Future Fund, which the text does not otherwise define. Rulemaking power under subsection (6) rests with the State Board of Education, while administration rests with the department. No amendment, repeal or other instrument is cited by name.
